name: dpf
description: Use when a diesel's particulate filter matters: DPF warning light, limp mode, low power, smoke, frequent regenerations or many short trips.
instructions: Call read_dpf {} once: it reads soot load and mass, ash, km since the last regeneration, regeneration count and exhaust temperature, and gives the assessed status.
Read the status line first, then the soot load; use the distance since regen and the regeneration count to judge how the car is driven.
When the status is regen-due or high, or the symptom is low power, also look at the fault codes (P2002, P2452-P2463 point to the DPF or its pressure sensor) before you recommend anything.
Values marked unconfirmed come from DIDs not yet checked on this car: quote them as indicative and say so.
interpret: Soot load bands (as assessDpf uses them): under 45 % ok (filter healthy); 45-69 % filling (normal, no action); 70-89 % regen-due; 90 % and above high (a forced or service regeneration may be needed).
Exhaust temperature at or above 500 °C with soot present means a regeneration is running now: the driver should keep driving at a steady speed and not switch off.
A regen needs 15–20 min above 60 km/h of steady driving; many short trips stop it from finishing, so soot keeps building.
Ash does not burn off in a regeneration: it only grows with age and mileage. A high ash load with a low soot load points to a worn filter, not to a missed regeneration.
Few km since the last regeneration together with a high regeneration count means the car regenerates very often: look for an underlying cause (EGR, injectors, a faulty pressure sensor, oil dilution).
Unconfirmed data never justifies an urgent verdict: an alarming unconfirmed value is a reason to check with a dedicated tool or a workshop, not proof of a blocked filter.
Status unknown means the car gave no soot reading: say that the filter could not be judged, not that it is fine.
